subject: Routing exception request + customer note for FinLytics latency spike
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: [Alert] FinLytics p99 spike + throughput drop in us-west (post-canary)

Hey team,

Quick summary from infra: during the midnight canary rollout of the new kernel-scheduler (build: ksched-1.14.0) we started to see elevated latency for a small set of customers. FinLytics is the largest affected tenant. Metrics: p50 ~ stable (~40ms), p95 jumped from 120ms -> 200ms, p99 jumped to ~900ms for a 20-minute window. Concurrently their sustained throughput to our serving tier dropped ~30% (requests still accepted but queuing observable).

Initial triage notes:
- Canary began 2027-03-21 00:12 PDT to 5% of traffic for that model family.
- KV cache hit rates unchanged; no memory pressure on the pool.
- Kernel sched trace attached (engine-trace-20270321.log).
- Hypothesis: scheduler change interacts badly with sequence-length distribution for FinLytics prompting preemption spikes and degraded batching behavior.

Asks:
1) Can we apply an immediate routing exception for FinLytics to move traffic to the reserved pool (us-west-dedicated-01) or fallback to the previous kernel binary for their traffic? Which is lower risk?
2) Is a canary pause / rollback advisable right now?

I will continue analyzing traces; tagging Sean to handle policy changes if we decide to reroute.

Marissa Cole
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: engine-trace-20270321.log

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Alert] FinLytics p99 spike + throughput drop in us-west (post-canary)

Thanks Marissa — and apologies to FinLytics if they're seeing user impact.

High level asks from my side (sales/CS):
- We need a concise customer-facing note ASAP (one paragraph + bullet impact + mitigation + next steps). Laura, can you draft?
- For mitigation: routing exception or fallback — which one is fastest to execute with lowest chance of collateral impact? I want the shortest path to restore their SLA.
- If we do a routing exception, give me the rollback criteria and estimated time to restore.

Jonas / Product: if we have a known incompatibility with the new scheduler, we need clarity on a rollback window or a fix timeline so I can set expectations with the FinLytics CTO.

I'll hold off external comms until we have the one-paragraph note.

Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Alert] FinLytics p99 spike + throughput drop in us-west (post-canary)

Thanks for flagging. A couple product points to consider:

- The scheduler change was intended to improve batching across mixed-sequence workloads; if it regresses for specific sequence distributions we can either: (A) pause/rollback canary globally for that model family, or (B) apply per-tenant kernel pinning/route exception.
- Per-tenant pinning is safe but it bumps maintenance overhead; we should prefer routing to a compatible pool if available.
- If we rollback the canary, what's our plan for validation before reintroducing? We should add an additional QA step for sequence-distribution testing to the rollout pipeline.

For now: prioritize minimal blast radius. If Sean can confirm a per-tenant routing rule with immediate effect, I support that while we complete the postmortem.

-Jonas
Product Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Alert] FinLytics p99 spike + throughput drop in us-west (post-canary)

We can implement a routing exception now. Proposed steps (estimate 10-15 minutes to enact, additional 30 minutes to observe):
1) Create policy 'route:finlytics-uswest-exception-20270321' that pins FinLytics model calls to us-west-dedicated-01 (older kernel binary still present).
2) Update the routing config and warm the host pool (preload cache buckets for their prefix where feasible).
3) Enable elevated telemetry for FinLytics (higher-resolution p99 / qps) and page SRE if regressions persist.
4) If p99 doesn't recover to within target (p99 < 250ms) within 45 minutes, we will rollback policy and revert to global throttle/rollback plan.

I'll start creating the policy and notify infra to prioritize the warmup. I'll attach the routing patch for review (routing-policy-change.patch).

--Sean Gallagher
Ops Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, adele.chen@finlytics.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 10:33:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: Customer note for FinLytics (please review)

Adele / FinLytics team —

We detected elevated latency for some requests to your production endpoints earlier today and acted immediately to mitigate impact. Fast facts: p99 latency briefly spiked and sustained throughput dropped for approximately 20 minutes starting at 00:12 PDT. Our engineering team identified a canary change to our scheduling kernel as the likely cause and applied a targeted routing exception to route your traffic to a dedicated pool running the prior, stable kernel.

What we did:
- Identified and isolated the affected traffic.
- Applied a per-tenant routing exception so your traffic is handled by a stable pool.
- Monitored and confirmed that p99 and throughput returned to normal.

Next steps:
- We're completing a postmortem and will share the technical findings by 03/24.
- We are offering a service credit for the impacted window; I'll follow up with details.
- If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk through the incident and answer technical questions (proposed: Tue 03/23 11:00 PDT).

We sincerely apologize for the disruption. We take reliability seriously and will share the root cause and remediation plan as soon as it’s available.

—Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: customer-note-draft.docx

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: adele.chen@finlytics.com, ops@finlytics.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: FinLytics update: routing exception applied, p99 restored — next steps

Team / Adele — quick status update and next steps.

Status:
- Sean applied 'route:finlytics-uswest-exception-20270321' on 2027-03-21 10:15 PDT; warmup completed.
- Monitoring shows p99 for FinLytics returned to ~110-140ms and throughput returned to baseline within 30 minutes of reroute.
- No collateral regressions observed for other tenants after policy change.

Actions completed:
- Targeted routing exception applied and validated.
- SRE collected traces and logs (engine-trace-20270321.log attached).
- CS (Laura) prepared customer note and offered a credit; Laura to handle credit/comms.

Open items / next steps:
1) Product (Jonas) to coordinate a rollback vs fix plan for ksched-1.14.0 and add sequence-distribution tests to rollout pipeline (requested ETA: 72 hours for a roadmap & mitigation plan).
2) SRE to finish full postmortem and share by 2027-03-24 (Marissa owner).
3) Schedule a customer call (Laura will confirm availability; proposed Tue 03/23 11:00 PDT).
4) Sales: I will confirm any credit / commercial ask with Adele and include DL-2027-1934 in our renewal notes.

Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. Recommend we include the incident as a 'routing-exception' case in the runbook so this path is clear for future per-tenant issues.

Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
